title: Make every interview count: Advice from the Pitney Bowes Talent Acquisition team
summary: Get advice from Pitney Bowes Talent Acquisition team, including tips on applications, interviews, storytelling, and standing out as a candidate.
body_markdown:
Whether you're searching for your first role or your next big move, the job hunt can feel like a lot to navigate. Here's the good news: the people on the other side of the table want you to succeed.


An interview is a two-way conversation, a chance to show who you are and what you'd bring to the team, and to find out whether the role is right for you. So, we went straight to the source. We asked members of our Talent Acquisition team, the people who review applications, search for talent, and guide candidates through the process every day, to share the advice they wish every candidate knew.


# 1. Make your profile and applications work for you


Recruiters don't just wait for applications to come in, so standing out can start before you ever click "apply."


Make sure your resume and LinkedIn profile clearly showcase your skills, accomplishments, and experience. When applying for a role, take time to tailor your application by highlighting the qualifications and achievements that are most relevant to the position.
